record.paper_title: Selected Open Problems in Discrete Geometry and Optimization
record.original_question: Let S^d be the d-dimensional unit sphere in E^(d+1), with d >= 2. A spherically convex body is a closed spherically convex subset of S^d with interior points that lies in a closed hemisphere, equivalently the intersection of S^d with a proper closed convex cone in E^(d+1). Its inradius r(K) is the spherical radius of the largest spherical ball contained in K. If spherically convex bodies K_1,...,K_n cover a spherical ball B of radius r(B) < pi/2 in S^d, must sum_{i=1}^n r(K_i) >= r(B)?

evidence.quote: Recall that Sd stands for the d-dimensional unit sphere in (d+1)-dimensional Euclidean space Ed+1; d >= 2. A spherically convex body is a closed, spherically convex subset K of Sd with interior points and lying in some closed hemisphere. The inradius r(K) of K is the spherical radius of the largest spherical ball contained in K. Question 3. Let the spherically convex bodies K1,...,Kn cover the spherical ball B of radius r(B) < pi/2 in Sd; d >= 2. Then prove or disprove that sum r(Ki) >= r(B).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^d \subset \mathbb{R}^{d+1}$ denote the $d$-dimensional unit sphere, with $d \ge 2$. A spherically convex body is a closed, spherically convex subset $K \subset S^d$ that has nonempty interior and is contained in some closed hemisphere; equivalently, $K = C \cap S^d$ for some proper closed convex cone $C \subset \mathbb{R}^{d+1}$. For two points $x,y \in S^d$, the spherical distance $d_S(x,y)$ is the angle between them (their geodesic distance on $S^d$). A spherical ball of center $c \in S^d$ and spherical radius $\rho \in (0,\pi)$ is the set $\{x \in S^d : d_S(x,c) \le \rho\}$. The inradius $r(K)$ of a spherically convex body $K$ is the supremum of the spherical radii of spherical balls contained in $K$.

Suppose that spherically convex bodies $K_1, \ldots, K_n \subset S^d$ cover a spherical ball $B \subset S^d$ of spherical radius $r(B) < \pi/2$, i.e., $B \subseteq \bigcup_{i=1}^n K_i$. Prove or disprove that
$$\sum_{i=1}^n r(K_i) \;\ge\; r(B).$$
artifact.status_search_result: Bezdek and Schneider (2010/2011, "Covering Large Balls with Convex Sets in Spherical Space") proved the analogous inequality for spherical caps of radius $\alpha \ge \pi/2$ (and for the entire sphere, with bound $\pi$). The case of small spherical balls with $r(B) < \pi/2$ does not appear to be covered by their result, and no later resolution was found in the search results, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Covering Large Balls with Convex Sets in Spherical Space
status_evidence.snippet: If a cap of spherical radius α ≥ π/2 is covered by a finite family of spherically convex bodies in S^{d-1}, d>2, then the sum of the inradii is at least α; if the whole sphere is covered, the sum is at least π.
status_evidence.claim: Resolves the analogous inequality only for caps of spherical radius at least π/2, leaving the small-ball case (r(B)<π/2) outside the established result.

status_evidence.title: Packing and Covering (Handbook of Discrete and Computational Geometry chapter)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey references the Bezdek–Schneider inradii inequality for spherical coverings without indicating extension to small balls.
status_evidence.claim: No more recent resolution of the small spherical ball case is reported in standard surveys.
